words.gloss: having the nature of waning / later stage

literal: Having the nature of fullness is the friendship of those of noble character; having the nature of the moon's later stage is the friendship of fools.
translation: The friendship of those of noble character is like the waxing moon that grows to fullness; the friendship of fools is like the waning moon that gradually fades away.
modern: அறிவுடையோரின் நட்பு வளர்பிறை போல வளரும் தன்மை உடையது; அறிவிலிகளின் நட்பு தேய்பிறை போலத் தேயும் தன்மை உடையது.
explanation: This couplet compares the nature of friendship to the phases of the moon. The friendship of wise and noble people (நீரவர்) is like the waxing moon (நிறைநீர), which starts small but steadily grows to complete fullness. In contrast, the friendship of foolish or ignorant people (பேதையார்) is like the waning moon (பிறைமதிப் பின்னீர), which may start large and bright but gradually diminishes until it disappears entirely. True friendship grows with time and understanding, while superficial friendship fades away.
